title: Barrierefreiheit / DB Red and DB Red 500
slide_intent: Separate identity red from functional contrast needs so recognition and readable interaction can coexist.
strategic_value: Context-specific red choices can help DB retain its identity while making text and controls easier to read.
demonstration: Logo/sleeper identity specimens use DB Red; a darker DB Red 500 accompanies button and label specimens, followed by three stated contrast pairings.
practical_value: Choose the red by foreground/background role and add a noncolor cue to links, warnings and notices.

content_islands.name: Identity red
content_islands.spec: Pair the DB logo and sleeper with the #FF002B swatch.

content_islands.name: Functional red
content_islands.spec: Pair the UI specimens with DB Red 500 #EC0016 and its contrasting-use explanation.

content_islands.name: Contrast and coding
content_islands.spec: Compare the three Aa pairings with their printed ratios and the double-coding instruction below.

reference_purposes.Intent: The source explicitly connects color decisions to access, legibility and contrast.
reference_purposes.Application: The page compares DB Red on Cold Black, DB Red 500 on White and White on DB Red 500.
reference_purposes.Constraint: Red text is limited to links, warnings and notices and must have an additional visual cue; White text on red uses DB Red 500.

ingredient.name: Identity and interface red
ingredient.role: Retain red recognition while providing context-appropriate text contrast.
ingredient.application: Use #EC0016 for the stated red UI grounds and red-on-white text, and #FF002B for red text on Cold Black; supplement color with another cue.
ingredient.scope: Source reports contrast ratios 4.8:1 and 4.6:1. Its limited red-text permission differs from the later general do/don’t wording; preserve the specific UI context rather than extending it to campaign typography.
